models_evaluated: six general-purpose LLMs (others not named in the text)

links.outcome: LLM ICD-10 coding agreement with human reference on real-world clinical notes
links.effect: Best model GPT-4o reached micro-F1 0.36 at three-character level and 0.15 at leaf level against the human reference.
links.quote: Even the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieved only modest agreement with the human reference, with micro-F1 scores of 0.36 at the three-character level and 0.15 at the leaf level.

links.outcome: Reliability of human reference standard for coding, measured via blinded clinician validation
links.effect: Human-coded references achieved precision 0.77 versus 0.59 for the strongest model; F1 conflates model error with human disagreement.
links.quote: In clinician validation, human-coded references achieved a precision of 0.77, compared to 0.59 for the strongest model, revealing a substantial gap between automated predictions and clinically accepted codes.

unlisted_practices: Portuguese-to-English translation of inputs (no consistent gains)
Lightweight supervised fine-tuning on code-description pairs (no accuracy improvement)

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM performance for automated ICD-10 coding against human clinician validation and reference standards on retrospective clinical notes, without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment workflow practice.
